papers.title: ShadoNet: A Cell Detection and Classification Framework for Ki-67 Pathology Images
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate detection and classification of individual cells are essential for quantitative histopathology. In Ki-67-based tumor grading, the clinically relevant index is calculated from immunopositive and immunonegative tumor cells, while non-tumor cells should be excluded. This is challenging because Ki-67-stained tumor regions often contain a heterogeneous mixture of immunopositive tumor cells, immunonegative tumor cells, and non-tumor cells. Here, we study cell detection and classification in Ki-67-stained histopathology images to support grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs), where reliable tumor-cell-specific identification is critical for tumor grading and decision-making. Results We present ShadoNet, a U-Net–style encoder–decoder framework that integrates shape priors with structured regression for cell detection and classification. ShadoNet predicts class-specific proximity maps that emphasize cell centers and jointly encode spatial location, morphology, and class identity through smooth intensity decay from cell centers. Across multiple Ki-67-stained histopathology datasets, incorporating shape information improved performance on standard detection and classification metrics, indicating that shape-derived priors provide useful class-related cues—without requiring full instance-level boundary annotations. Availability and Implementation ShadoNet uses the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate initial cellular shape masks, which are refined using human-annotated nuclear point labels to construct ground-truth proximity maps. During training, shape guidance is enforced via two auxiliary objectives: (i) a rotation-extended Scaled IoU (SIoU) loss to capture orientation and shape alignment, and (ii) a Hausdorff Distance Transform (HDT) loss to penalize boundary discrepancies between predictions and ground truth. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/GhasemiGOF/ShadoNet . A fixed version of the code used for the experiments in this manuscript has been archived at Zenodo with DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21050210 . BCData and SHIDC-B-Ki-67 are publicly available datasets and can be accessed through their original publications

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在定量组织病理学中，准确检测与分类单个细胞至关重要。在基于Ki-67的肿瘤分级系统中，临床相关指标是通过计算免疫阳性及免疫阴性的肿瘤细胞得出的，同时必须排除非肿瘤细胞。然而这一过程颇具挑战性，因为经过Ki-67染色的肿瘤区域通常包含免疫阳性肿瘤细胞、免疫阴性肿瘤细胞以及非肿瘤细胞的混合体。本研究旨在探讨如何在Ki-67染色的组织病理学图像中实现细胞检测与分类，以辅助胰腺神经内分泌肿瘤的分级工作——在这一过程中，可靠地识别肿瘤细胞对于分级决策具有决定性意义。  

**结果**  
我们提出了ShadoNet这一基于U-Net结构的编码器-解码器框架，该框架结合了形状先验信息与结构化回归算法，用于细胞的检测与分类。ShadoNet能够生成突出显示细胞中心的类别特异性邻近图谱，并通过细胞中心处强度的逐渐减弱来同时编码细胞的空间位置、形态特征及其所属类别。在多个经过Ki-67染色的组织病理学数据集上进行测试后发现，加入形状信息显著提升了检测与分类的准确率，这说明基于形状的先验信息能够为分类提供有用的线索——而无需依赖完整的实例级边界标注。  

**实现方式**  
ShadoNet利用Segment Anything Model（SAM）生成初始的细胞形状掩膜，随后通过人工标注的核点标签对这些掩膜进行精细化处理，从而构建出真实的邻近图谱。在训练过程中，通过两个辅助目标来实现对细胞形状的引导：(i) 采用旋转扩展的Scaled IoU损失函数来评估方向与形状的对齐程度；(ii) 使用Hausdorff距离变换损失函数来惩罚预测结果与真实数据之间的边界差异。相关代码已公开发布在https://github.com/GhasemiGOF/ShadoNet，而用于本研究的固定版本代码则存档于Zenodo数据库，其DOI号为https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21050210。BCData与SHIDC-B-Ki-67也是公开可用的数据集，可通过相关学术文献获取。

papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound−protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The identification of compound–protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy. Results We propose DESTIN (dual structure-guided estimation of substance–target interaction networks), an ML framework for CPI prediction on a genome-wide scale from the three-dimensional (3D) structures of compounds and proteins. We constructed compound feature vectors that spatially reflect stable 3D conformations from a quantum–chemical perspective by fine-tuning a 3D structure-based foundation model. Furthermore, we constructed protein feature vectors leveraging sequence-based structure representations and protein language models, even for proteins that do not have 3D structures determined experimentally. CPI prediction was performed using an integrative ML model on 3D structure-aware feature vectors for compounds and proteins. The effectiveness of the proposed model was validated via rigorous benchmark tests on practical scenarios. DESTIN exhibited good predictive performance, even for structurally complex and pharmacologically important membrane proteins. These results show that DESTIN is promising for various pharmaceutical applications. Availability All source code and data supporting this study are publicly available on GitHub and archived on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21759701 )

在药物发现的早期阶段，识别化合物与蛋白质之间的相互作用至关重要。然而，基于一维或二维表示的机器学习方法无法捕捉这些相互作用位点上的关键几何信息，从而导致其预测精度受限。因此，我们提出了DESTIN这一框架——该框架利用化合物与蛋白质的三维结构，通过机器学习方法在基因组范围内预测这类相互作用。我们首先通过微调基于三维结构的基模型，构建了能够从量子化学角度反映化合物稳定三维构象的特征向量；同时，也利用基于序列的结构信息及蛋白质语言模型为蛋白质生成相应的特征向量——即便这些蛋白质尚未通过实验确定其三维结构。最终，我们使用整合型机器学习模型，结合化合物与蛋白质的三维结构特征向量进行相互作用预测。实际测试表明，DESTIN在预测结构复杂且具有药理意义的膜蛋白相互作用方面表现优异，这一结果进一步证明了其在药物研究中的巨大潜力。

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.

RESULTS: We propose DESTIN (dual structure-guided estimation of substance-target interaction networks), an ML framework for CPI prediction on a genome-wide scale from the three-dimensional (3D) structures of compounds and proteins. We constructed compound feature vectors that spatially reflect stable 3D conformations from a quantum-chemical perspective by fine-tuning a 3D structure-based foundation model. Furthermore, we constructed protein feature vectors leveraging sequence-based structure representations and protein language models, even for proteins that do not have 3D structures determined experimentally. CPI prediction was performed using an integrative ML model on 3D structure-aware feature vectors for compounds and proteins. The effectiveness of the proposed model was validated via rigorous benchmark tests on practical scenarios. DESTIN exhibited good predictive performance, even for structurally complex and pharmacologically important membrane proteins. These results show that DESTIN is promising for various pharmaceutical applications.

AVAILABILITY: All source code and data supporting this study are publicly available on GitHub and archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21759701).

papers.title: CircadiOmics: bioinformatics platform for circadian rhythms
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Circadian rhythms are fundamental to biology: they occur at the molecular level across all species and are critical to homeostasis and biological functions. They are also essential for health and medicine, as disruption of circadian regulation has been linked to numerous health problems, and many drug targets exhibit circadian oscillations, highlighting the importance of molecular-level circadian insight for precision medicine. Despite the rapid growth of circadian omic time series datasets, informatics tools for processing and analyzing this growing wealth of data remain limited. Results CircadiOmics provides, to the best of our knowledge, the largest repository and analytical platform for circadian omic data, consisting primarily of transcriptomic data, along with metabolomic, proteomic, and acetylomic datasets. CircadiOmics contains 704 omic datasets across 18 species, 30 tissue/organ categories, and 21 experiment types, including genetic manipulations, dietary interventions, and disease-associated conditions. By leveraging this repository, users can access an environment for comparing and visualizing molecular-level circadian oscillations. Periodicity statistics computed using BIO_CYCLE, including period, amplitude, phase, p -values, and q -values, are available as interactive plots and downloadable tables. This updated version of CircadiOmics introduces new features and substantially expanded data coverage, establishing it as a comprehensive resource for the exploration and analysis of circadian omic data. Availability and implementation CircadiOmics is freely accessible at: https://circadiomics.igb.uci.edu . The source code for BIO_CYCLE is available on GitHub: https://github.com/BaldiLab/BIO_CYCLE and archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22108329

**摘要**  
生物节律是生物学的基础现象：它们在所有物种的分子层面普遍存在，对维持机体稳态与执行各种生物功能至关重要。这些节律也与健康与医学密切相关——节律紊乱会引发诸多健康问题，而许多药物的作用靶点也表现出节律性变化，这进一步凸显了从分子层面理解生物节律对于精准医疗的重要性。尽管与生物节律相关的数据序列资源正在迅速增加，但用于处理和分析这些数据的生物信息学工具仍然较为有限。

all_papers.title: ShadoNet: A Cell Detection and Classification Framework for Ki-67 Pathology Images
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Accurate detection and classification of individual cells are essential for quantitative histopathology. In Ki-67-based tumor grading, the clinically relevant index is calculated from immunopositive and immunonegative tumor cells, while non-tumor cells should be excluded. This is challenging because Ki-67-stained tumor regions often contain a heterogeneous mixture of immunopositive tumor cells, immunonegative tumor cells, and non-tumor cells. Here, we study cell detection and classification in Ki-67-stained histopathology images to support grading of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PanNETs), where reliable tumor-cell-specific identification is critical for tumor grading and decision-making. Results We present ShadoNet, a U-Net–style encoder–decoder framework that integrates shape priors with structured regression for cell detection and classification. ShadoNet predicts class-specific proximity maps that emphasize cell centers and jointly encode spatial location, morphology, and class identity through smooth intensity decay from cell centers. Across multiple Ki-67-stained histopathology datasets, incorporating shape information improved performance on standard detection and classification metrics, indicating that shape-derived priors provide useful class-related cues—without requiring full instance-level boundary annotations. Availability and Implementation ShadoNet uses the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to generate initial cellular shape masks, which are refined using human-annotated nuclear point labels to construct ground-truth proximity maps. During training, shape guidance is enforced via two auxiliary objectives: (i) a rotation-extended Scaled IoU (SIoU) loss to capture orientation and shape alignment, and (ii) a Hausdorff Distance Transform (HDT) loss to penalize boundary discrepancies between predictions and ground truth. Code is publicly available at: https://github.com/GhasemiGOF/ShadoNet . A fixed version of the code used for the experiments in this manuscript has been archived at Zenodo with DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21050210 . BCData and SHIDC-B-Ki-67 are publicly available datasets and can be accessed through their original publications

MOTIVATION: Accurate detection and classification of individual cells are essential for quantitative histopathology. In Ki-67-based tumor grading, the clinically relevant index is calculated from immunopositive and immunonegative tumor cells, while non-tumor cells should be excluded. This is challenging because Ki-67-stained tumor regions often contain a heterogeneous mixture of immunopositive tumor cells, immunonegative tumor cells, and non-tumor cells. RESULTS: We present ShadoNet, a U-Net-style encoder-decoder framework that integrates shape priors with structured regression for cell detection and classification. ShadoNet predicts class-specific proximity maps that emphasize cell centers and jointly encode spatial location, morphology, and class identity through smooth intensity decay from cell centers. Across multiple Ki-67-stained histopathology datasets, incorporating shape information improved performance on standard detection and classification metrics, indicating that shape-derived priors provide useful class-related cues-without requiring full instance-level boundary annotations.

all_papers.title: Genome-wide-scale prediction of compound−protein interactions using foundation and language models based on three-dimensional structures of compounds and proteins
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation The identification of compound–protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy. Results We propose DESTIN (dual structure-guided estimation of substance–target interaction networks), an ML framework for CPI prediction on a genome-wide scale from the three-dimensional (3D) structures of compounds and proteins. We constructed compound feature vectors that spatially reflect stable 3D conformations from a quantum–chemical perspective by fine-tuning a 3D structure-based foundation model. Furthermore, we constructed protein feature vectors leveraging sequence-based structure representations and protein language models, even for proteins that do not have 3D structures determined experimentally. CPI prediction was performed using an integrative ML model on 3D structure-aware feature vectors for compounds and proteins. The effectiveness of the proposed model was validated via rigorous benchmark tests on practical scenarios. DESTIN exhibited good predictive performance, even for structurally complex and pharmacologically important membrane proteins. These results show that DESTIN is promising for various pharmaceutical applications. Availability All source code and data supporting this study are publicly available on GitHub and archived on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21759701 )

我们提出了DESTIN这一机器学习框架，该框架能够利用化合物和蛋白质的三维结构，在全基因组范围内预测它们之间的相互作用。通过微调基于三维结构的基模型，我们构建了能够从量子化学角度反映化合物稳定三维构象的特征向量；对于那些尚未通过实验确定其三维结构的蛋白质，我们也利用基于序列的结构信息及蛋白质语言模型来生成其特征向量。最终，我们采用集成机器学习模型，对这些特征向量进行处理以进行相互作用预测。实际测试表明，DESTIN在预测结构复杂且具有药理意义的膜蛋白相互作用方面表现优异，这一结果进一步证明了该模型的实用价值。

数据与代码公开情况：本研究的所有源代码及相关数据均已公开发布在GitHub上，并存档于Zenodo平台（链接：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21759701）。

补充信息：更多补充数据可在线查阅Bioinformatics数据库。
all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: The identification of compound-protein interactions (CPIs) is crucial in the early stages of drug discovery. However, machine-learning (ML)-based methods based on one- and two-dimensional representations cannot capture important geometric information on the binding sites of CPIs, which limits their predictive accuracy.

RESULTS: We propose DESTIN (dual structure-guided estimation of substance-target interaction networks), an ML framework for CPI prediction on a genome-wide scale from the three-dimensional (3D) structures of compounds and proteins. We constructed compound feature vectors that spatially reflect stable 3D conformations from a quantum-chemical perspective by fine-tuning a 3D structure-based foundation model. Furthermore, we constructed protein feature vectors leveraging sequence-based structure representations and protein language models, even for proteins that do not have 3D structures determined experimentally. CPI prediction was performed using an integrative ML model on 3D structure-aware feature vectors for compounds and proteins. The effectiveness of the proposed model was validated via rigorous benchmark tests on practical scenarios. DESTIN exhibited good predictive performance, even for structurally complex and pharmacologically important membrane proteins. These results show that DESTIN is promising for various pharmaceutical applications.

AVAILABILITY: All source code and data supporting this study are publicly available on GitHub and archived on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21759701).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.title: CircadiOmics: bioinformatics platform for circadian rhythms
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Circadian rhythms are fundamental to biology: they occur at the molecular level across all species and are critical to homeostasis and biological functions. They are also essential for health and medicine, as disruption of circadian regulation has been linked to numerous health problems, and many drug targets exhibit circadian oscillations, highlighting the importance of molecular-level circadian insight for precision medicine. Despite the rapid growth of circadian omic time series datasets, informatics tools for processing and analyzing this growing wealth of data remain limited. Results CircadiOmics provides, to the best of our knowledge, the largest repository and analytical platform for circadian omic data, consisting primarily of transcriptomic data, along with metabolomic, proteomic, and acetylomic datasets. CircadiOmics contains 704 omic datasets across 18 species, 30 tissue/organ categories, and 21 experiment types, including genetic manipulations, dietary interventions, and disease-associated conditions. By leveraging this repository, users can access an environment for comparing and visualizing molecular-level circadian oscillations. Periodicity statistics computed using BIO_CYCLE, including period, amplitude, phase, p -values, and q -values, are available as interactive plots and downloadable tables. This updated version of CircadiOmics introduces new features and substantially expanded data coverage, establishing it as a comprehensive resource for the exploration and analysis of circadian omic data. Availability and implementation CircadiOmics is freely accessible at: https://circadiomics.igb.uci.edu . The source code for BIO_CYCLE is available on GitHub: https://github.com/BaldiLab/BIO_CYCLE and archived on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22108329

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
生物节律是生物学的基础现象：它们在所有物种的分子层面普遍存在，对维持机体稳态与执行各种生物功能至关重要。这些节律也与健康与医学密切相关——节律紊乱会引发诸多健康问题，而许多药物的作用靶点也表现出节律性变化，这进一步凸显了从分子层面理解生物节律对于精准医疗的重要性。尽管与生物节律相关的数据序列资源正在迅速增加，但用于处理和分析这些数据的生物信息学工具仍然较为有限。  

**结果**  
据我们所知，CircadiOmics是目前规模最大的生物节律组学数据存储与分析平台。该平台主要收录转录组数据，同时还包含代谢组、蛋白质组及乙酰化组学数据。目前，CircadiOmics涵盖了18种物种、30种组织/器官类型以及21种实验类型（包括基因操作、饮食干预及疾病相关研究），共收集了704个组学数据集。用户可以利用这一平台对比并可视化分子层面的节律变化；通过BIO_cycle工具计算得出的周期性参数（如周期长度、振幅、相位、p值和q值）会以交互式图表或可下载表格的形式呈现。此次更新后的CircadiOmics新增了大量功能，数据覆盖范围也得到了显著扩展，使其成为探索与分析生物节律组学数据的理想资源。  

**获取方式与技术支持**  
CircadiOmics可免费访问：https://circadiomics.igb.uci.edu；BIO_cycle工具的源代码可在GitHub上获取：https://github.com/BaldiLab/BIO_CYCLE，同时也在Zenodo平台上进行了存档：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22108329。
